name: Seven-touch email and LinkedIn
when_to_use: Email and LinkedIn are both wired and the ICP is genuinely reachable on both. Do not select it because it is bigger: an unwired channel in the plan is a hole, not a touch.
rationale: The channels do different jobs. Email carries the context, the LinkedIn connection makes the sender a real person before the second email lands, and the DM only works once connection is accepted. Sequences across 3+ channels report 287% more responses than single-channel, but the number is a vendor benchmark and the mechanism - repeated recognition from a face rather than an address - is the part to trust.
cites: research/01 (multichannel 287% figure, Outbound Sales Pro - vendor-published)
evidence_note: The 287% uplift is vendor-published and uncontrolled. Treat the ordering as the durable part, not the multiplier.

send_window.why: Materialized at send time against the contact's location.

channel_limits.linkedin_connect: ~100 connection requests per week on a standard account
channel_limits.note: A campaign whose touch-2 volume exceeds this is not sendable as planned. gtme-sequence checks it against the list size before the gate.

touches.intent: Name the problem in the reader's own words and earn one reply.
Become a face rather than an address, before the second email arrives. Recognition is the whole job here.
constraints: no note, or one line referencing the email
never pitch in a connection request
cites: research/01 (day-2 connection request, no note or brief email reference)

touches.intent: Add an angle touch 1 did not use.
cites: research/04 §5.2 (each follow-up adds a new angle)

touches.intent: Use the accepted connection. Shorter and more direct than email, because the reader already knows the name.
constraints: skip entirely if the connection was not accepted - never DM into a pending request
cites: research/01 (day-6 InMail or DM if connected)

touches.intent: Answer the objection this persona actually raises, before it is voiced.
constraints: only raise an objection the offer can answer

touches.intent: Close the loop and make not-replying easy.
One final, low-cost close on the channel where a non-reply costs the least.

branches.why: Any reply cancels the cold sequence, on every channel - not just the one they replied on.
